title: 1,368 AI Failures and What They Teach About Evals — Vishal Srivastava & Tanmay Sah, New York Life
talk_summary: The speakers analyzed 1,368 incidents from the AI Incident Database and found failures cluster into 13 dimensions across development, deployment, and business context, with deployment controls most associated with harm. They propose failure-driven, risk-based system-level evals that test the whole deployment setup (tools, human review, permissions, recovery) rather than just the model, and treat the evaluator itself as something to validate.

takeaways.what_they_do: Start from the system's explicit claims, actively try to break them with adversarial scenarios, then either restrict the system from the failing region or add a control (policy check, human escalation), and retest to confirm the control catches the error.
takeaways.evidence_quote: any evaluation that needs to be done has to falsify, not to confirm

takeaways.technique: Test the evaluator, not just the artifact
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the LLM judge/reviewer as part of the governed system: check whether the evaluator is reliable, what evidence it covers, and whether it applies to the deployed system, since judges make mistakes and tests miss failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is where we need to check whether the evaluator is reliable, what the evidence covers

takeaways.what_they_do: Decompose risk into frequency of model failure, whether it reaches a real decision, whether it goes uncaught, and severity; deployment controls (human mediation, monitoring, exposure, authority) were more associated with harm than technical model failure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: controls that we have in deployment are more critically associated with harm
takeaways.numbers: deployment controls ranked above business impact and technical failure; ~6 sub-dimensions per incident on average

takeaways.technique: Test agent boundaries, tool failure, and recovery
takeaways.what_they_do: Extend eval scope to the deployment system: does retrieval return the right info, what happens when a tool fails, does the agent stay within permissions, and can the system recover.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what happens when a tool fails? Does human review catch mistake? Or does the agent stay within its permission or boundary?

takeaways.technique: Materiality ranking to allocate eval/review effort
takeaways.what_they_do: Score each AI use case on a materiality scale (financial impact, legal consequence, number of users affected) and spend review/eval resources only on high-materiality cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can allocate more resources to much higher material AI use cases
